items.text: Subscribers are the one fragile check: 0.6 per 1,000 views, from an older finished episode, against a usual 2.8. In E8, DesignerTom gained 26 subscribers and Dive Club gained 12.
items.recommendation: Add a spoken subscribe ask about halfway in and a pinned comment on both channels. Watch whether Dive Club, the weaker channel in E8, closes the gap. Change only this so the result is readable.

items.text: Live peak is 87 against a usual 97.5, and live average is 70 against 73. E9, a finished episode, reached 133 at peak and 109 on average, and each live viewer stayed 14.2 minutes.
items.recommendation: Build next week's live around what E9 had: viewer-submitted stories and prerecorded nominations early, and a soundboard moment later. Test one of them in the first half hour and compare the peak.

items.text: Fewer people pressed play on the announce: 25.6 against a usual 27.4. Across the show, end screens brought 19 YouTube views and playlists brought 309.
items.recommendation: Put an end screen pointing to the next episode on every upload and add each episode to a playlist this week. Post the announce with one strong guest clip instead of a bare link, then compare plays.

items.text: E6 lost 4.8 of every 100 viewers about a sixth of the way in, where the transcript shows a scramble to get avatars working on screen. LinkedIn viewers also wrote that they couldn't hear the caller.
items.recommendation: Run a full sound and screen check on every call-in guest and every new on-screen tool before going live. Keep any live setup short. Then compare the early drop in the next episode as a test.

items.text: Chat is the healthy part: 83.9 chatters for every 100 viewers against a usual 53.9, and 84.1 held to the last ten minutes against 66.4. E13 gained viewers about halfway in, during a hands-on walkthrough.
items.recommendation: Protect it: keep a hands-on walkthrough around the middle of each live and ask viewers to post their own setups in chat during it. Keep chat on screen so newcomers see people talking.
